title: Integral maximum flow

problem.name: Integral maximum flow
problem.statement_latex:
Given directed capacities $c_e\in\{0,\ldots,U\}$ and terminals $s,t$, maximize the net outflow from $s$ over $0\le f_e\le c_e$, subject to flow conservation at $V\setminus\{s,t\}$. This is a central network optimization primitive.
Complexity counts quantum time with coherent residual-graph access and classical RAM time for polynomially bounded integral capacities.

quantum.details_latex: This bound assumes $U\le n^{1/4}$. The flow is returned as an explicit classical edge array. Residual-capacity updates and subsequent coherent queries are part of the implementation.
quantum.details_text: This bound assumes $U\le n^{1/4}$. The flow is returned as an explicit classical edge array. Residual-capacity updates and subsequent coherent queries are part of the implementation.

classical.headline_latex: $m^{1+o(1)}$, Chen--Kyng--Liu--Peng--Probst Gutenberg--Sachdeva and deterministic van den Brand et al.
classical.details_latex: The almost-linear bound applies to polynomially bounded integer capacities. Interior-point optimization is combined with dynamic graph data structures for finding improving flow directions. This bound is asymptotically stronger than the displayed quantum blocking-flow bound for the same capacity regime.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant implementation uses $O(\log n+\log U)$ search and arithmetic registers plus oracle workspace. Residual-flow data occupy $O(m\log U)$ classical bits and must support coherent queries after updates.
